title: The cook who survived sixty hours inside a sunken ship
hook: A cook lived almost three days inside a sunken ship.
summary: In 2013 Nigerian cook Harrison Okene survived about sixty hours in an air pocket inside a capsized tugboat on the seabed, until divers searching for bodies saw his hand move.
sources: Wikipedia / BBC News: Harrison Okene, cook on tug Jascon-4, capsized off Nigeria 26 May 2013, about 30 m deep, found alive after roughly 60 hours
The Guardian and DCN Diving accounts: divers searching the wreck found him in an air pocket; 11 other crew died; he was decompressed in a chamber

lines.text: A cook lived almost three days inside a sunken ship.
lines.caps: A *cook lived | almost *three days | inside a *sunken ship

lines.text: In May twenty thirteen, a tugboat capsized off Nigeria.
Harrison Okene was aboard when it sank thirty metres.
lines.caps: *Harrison Okene | was *aboard | when it sank *thirty metres

lines.text: Eleven crew died. He was alone, in the dark.
lines.caps: *Eleven crew died. | He was *alone, | in the *dark

lines.text: He found a pocket of air and waited.
lines.caps: He found a *pocket of air | and *waited

lines.text: Days later, divers came only to search for bodies.
Then one of them saw a hand move.
After about sixty hours, he came up alive.
One small pocket of air was enough.

post.caption:
He was trapped in the dark, thirty metres down, and rescuers only expected to find bodies.
Could you have stayed calm for sixty hours?
